finalText:
Three weeks is the right length to do both sides of Patagonia properly, and December is peak season — long daylight, the full trail network open, and every refugio and bus seat booked out months ahead, so lock accommodation first and build the rest around it.

The logic of the route: fly into Punta Arenas, do the Chilean half first (the Torres del Paine W over five days, with iceberg kayaking on Lago Grey as your first paddle), recover in Puerto Natales, then cross the border by bus to El Calafate for Perito Moreno and on to El Chaltén for the Fitz Roy classics — Laguna de los Tres, Laguna Torre — and a second, wilder kayak on the Río de las Vueltas. One border crossing, no backtracking, and rest days placed exactly where your legs will demand them.

Be straight about December's one catch: the wind. Gusts over 100 km/h are normal, forecasts shift daily, and the Torres and Los Tres viewpoints are worth re-ordering around any calm morning — build the flexibility in rather than fighting it.

Estimated cost: £4,700 per person including international flights, buses, refugio half-board on the W, guided kayak sessions and park fees — inside your £5,000 budget. Want me to look at flight options into Punta Arenas and out of El Calafate, or firm up the refugio booking sequence?
